title: Redesign paged ranking envelopes and batchstream semantics for rerank API
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: The current reranking endpoint mixes streaming, page cursors, and top_k semantics in ways that make client implementation error-prone for large result sets and causes inconsistent latencies for batched rerank workloads. This ticket redesigns the request/response envelope ("paged ranking envelopes") and introduces an explicit batchstream mode to decouple per-request latency from large-K retrievals. Goals: improve ergonomics for clients, make pagination and stable continuation tokens deterministic across reranker variants, and reduce tail latency for high-concurrency embedding+rerank pipelines.
background:
Current issues observed in customer telemetry and internal benches:
- Clients request large top_k (K > 500) which spikes memory and increases per-request latency.
- Continuation tokens are opaque and can become invalid across model variant fallbacks.
- Streaming incremental outputs interleave with pagination metadata making it hard to consume partial results reliably.
- Batching embeddings+rerank end-to-end often couples tokenization/embedding latency to the reranker retrieval phase causing unpredictable SLO misses.
Telemetry links: (confluence/benchmarks/infra) - see notes_links. Service incidents: rerank-autoscale-2026-02-18 impacted p95 latency.
proposed_api_changes:
1) Introduce 'envelope' response object that separates: metadata (stable_result_id, request_id, provenance), page_info (page_index, page_size, continuation_cursor, shard_hint), and results (ordered list).
2) Rename/clarify 'top_k' to 'page_size' and add 'max_results_cap' for server-side enforcement.
3) Add 'batchstream' request mode: client can set mode=batchstream and a target_batch_size; server will return immediate ordered partial pages as they complete (non-blocking) with stable_result_id for later continuation.
4) Standardize continuation_cursor format to be: base64("version:stable_result_id:shard_checkpoint:offset") to survive model fallbacks and shard moves.
5) Streaming + pagination contract: stream frames MUST be full envelopes; consumers can resume by passing continuation_cursor to a follow-up call.
6) Add 'explain_scores' optional field to include lightweight provenance (reasoning tokens or vector distances) with size-limited sampling.
Example request (pseudo): {
  "query": "...",
  "candidates": ["id1","id2",...],
  "page_size": 100,
  "mode": "batchstream",
  "max_results_cap": 1000
}
backward_compatibility_migration:
- Default behavior for existing clients remains last-stable contract for 3 months.
- New 'mode' parameter is optional; if omitted server maps previous behavior to mode=blocking with page_size = top_k.
- Introduce a migration header 'X-Rerank-Contract: v2' that opts client into new semantics.
- Compatibility shim: incoming old-style continuation cursors are accepted and translated to v2 stable_result_id where possible (best-effort).
- Deprecation plan: log usage of legacy cursors and notify users via console and telemetry for 90 days before rejecting them.
acceptance_criteria: API schema published in SDKs and Console docs for rerank-2.0
Server implements envelope framing, stable_result_id and standardized continuation_cursor
Internal benchmarks show p95 latency improvement >= 20% for large-K batch workloads when using batchstream
End-to-end tests cover resume semantics across model fallback and shard rebalance
Migration header allows safe coexistence; no existing client errors in 2 weeks of canary traffic
design_decisions:
- Chose explicit 'mode' rather than implicit heuristics so clients can select latency vs completeness tradeoffs.
- continuation_cursor is versioned and signed (HMAC) to prevent accidental misuse; server rotates signing keys quarterly.
- We limit explain_scores payload to 5 items per result by default to bound response size.
- For batchstream we prioritize returning fully-scored top-of-shard pages to reduce perceived latency.
- We will not expose internal shard topology; shard_hint is advisory only.
- Reuse existing rate-limiting and quota enforcement; batchstream counts against same per-request units but allows partial early credits for returned pages.
implementation_tasks: API: add mode, page_size, max_results_cap, explain_scores parameters to rerank endpoint (ENG-52341.1)
Runtime: implement envelope marshalling & stable_result_id lifecycle (ENG-52341.2)
Runtime: implement batchstream scheduler and early-flush logic (ENG-52341.3)
Storage: persist minimal continuation checkpoints (shard_checkpoint + offset) for 7 days (ENG-52341.4)
SDK: add typed response envelopes and migration header support (ENG-52341.5)
Docs: update API reference, migration guide, and SDK examples (ENG-52341.6)
E2E: add integration tests for resume across model fallback and rebalance (ENG-52341.7)
Perf: add bench harness for embedding+rerank batchstream workloads (ENG-52341.8)
testing_plan: Unit tests for envelope encoder/decoder including malformed cursor rejection
Integration test: resume continuation_cursor after simulated shard move (mock storage)
Chaos test: model fallback path returns alternate variant -> ensure stable_result_id continuity
Load test: submit concurrent batchstream requests with page_size=200 and measure p50/p95/p99
Compatibility test: legacy clients without X-Rerank-Contract header should behave unchanged
Client SDK conformance tests to verify stream frames are full envelopes
rollout_plan:
Phase 1: internal alpha behind feature flag for rerank-v2 on dev clusters (2 engineers monitoring).
Phase 2: canary with 1% of production traffic for 7 days; enable logging of legacy cursor translation.
Phase 3: 25% traffic for 3 days, escalate to 100% if no regressions in latency/errors.
Phase 4: announce migration and deprecation schedule to customers, update Console toggles.
Rollback: feature flag kill switch; stable_result_id remains consultable to clean up partial results.

2026-03-05: Design review notes: crypto requirement added for cursor signing; UX team asked for stable_result_id to be visible in Console result inspector.
2026-03-08: SDK team opened draft PR for Python and TS clients that return Envelope objects and helper to resume by cursor.
2026-03-10: Running canary tests in staging; observed edge case when explain_scores combined with batchstream increases payload size past client limits — added size cap and sampling rule.
